repairs.text: Strongest feature: Aron Ra answers Hernandez’s particle-aggregate challenge with a concrete embodied alternative: personhood depends on integrated neural, bodily, endocrine, and experiential organization, so neither unchanged matter nor transferable mental information independently preserves the person. Principal limitation: Emergence identifies the relevant system but does not specify what makes that system numerically continuous through reorganization, while the differently embodied transfer example assumes the identity discontinuity it must establish. Live burden: Aron Ra must state a principled continuity condition that distinguishes development, endocrine change, impairment, gradual replacement, and wholesale transfer, then explain why integrated physical organization yields categorical person-status despite component divisibility. Locked score: The locked score of 77 remains warranted because the reply directly engages the aggregate model and supplies embodiment evidence, yet leaves persistence and emergence insufficiently explained.

Strongest feature: Hernandez turns Aron Ra’s embodied account into a precise persistence test by asking whether altered beliefs and memories mean that yesterday’s adult or the five-year-old child stopped existing instead of developing continuously. Principal limitation: The challenge sometimes recasts every mental alteration as replacement, although Aron Ra can invoke continuous embodied organization and history while limiting identity loss to sufficiently radical discontinuity. Live burden: Hernandez must demonstrate that the negative lacks a threshold, then show that an immaterial soul offers a clearer persistence criterion and is necessary, rather than asserted, for separating maturation, impairment, and replacement. Locked score: The locked score of 79 remains warranted because this highly responsive childhood-to-adulthood comparison exposes the missing criterion, while the further inference from that omission to a soul remains evidentially incomplete.
